paper_metadata.title: Deformation mechanism and mechanical properties of a thermomechanically processed β Ti–28Nb–35.4Zr alloy
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials

evidence.quote: The effects of thermomechanical treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of a newly developed β titanium alloy, i.e., Ti–28Nb–35.4Zr (wt%, hereafter denoted Ti–Nb–Zr) were investigated.
CP-Ti (grade 2), used as a reference group for the evaluation of the tensile mechanical properties, was tested under the same conditions as the Ti–Nb–Zr alloy specimens.

The dark field image derived from the ω and α” spots circled in Fig. 5c revealed that the size of ω particles is around ~12 nm.
Further TEM analysis indicated that the deformation band shown in Fig. 6a-b were a {332} twin and the stress-induced ω formed in the β {332} twins.
the CRST specimen showed recrystallized grains with grain size in the range of 50 ~ 150 µm after annealing.
The XRD pattern of the CRST specimen revealed peaks attributable to only a β phase; showing a recrystallized β phase without any sign of peaks belonging to other phases (Fig. 3f).

The CMO between the β matrix and deformation product for CR-1 was measured to be between 10° and 30° (Fig. 7d). Hence, the band structures shown in Fig. 7c can be evaluated as kink bands. Careful examination showed that the dominant deformation mechanism in CR-1 was the formation of kink bands.

formation of kink bands was the dominant deformation mechanism in CR-2 (Fig. 7e-f). The measured CMO between the β matrix and band structures in CR-2 was between 20° and 30° (Fig. 7f), indicating the formation of kink bands during CR.

The IPF map of CR-3 exhibited typical lentoid structures along with band-type structures (Fig. 7g). The measured CMO between the β matrix and lentoid structures was around 50.5° (Fig. 7h). It has been reported that CMO between a matrix structure and {332}<113> twin is ~50.5° along <110>β direction (Furuta et al., 2005). Thus, the lentoid structures marked with a dotted white arrow in Fig. 7g were {332}<113> twins.

The black features in Figs. 7g and 7j were shear bands originated by the distorted crystals which led to poor indexing rate. Kink bands and {332}<113> twins were separated by the shear bands (Figs. 7g and 7j). Shear bands, kink bands and {332}<113> twins were found in CR-3.
The deformation mechanisms evolved from kink bands and {332}<113> twins to dominant shear band formations and distorted {332}<113> twins as observed in CR-4 (Figs. 7j and 7k).
